title: Canonical finite-free tensor comparison for derived products and strict towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $a:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ as an $R$-module sheaf for a finite integer $d\geq0$. Use the unbounded module derived categories $D(R),D(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $C=-\otimes_R^L S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $\operatorname{Tow}(R)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R))$, and similarly for $S$. Let $C^{\operatorname{Tow}}:D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(S))$ be induced by termwise tensor, which is exact under the finite-free hypothesis. Write $L_R,L_S$ for total right derived inverse limit with its functorial Roos triangles [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

For every countable family $(M_n)$ in $D(R)$, the canonical projection comparison $C(\prod_n^D M_n)\to\prod_n^D C(M_n)$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_X:C L_R X\xrightarrow{\sim}L_S C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\qquad(X\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))).$$
It is the total derived-functor comparison induced by the ordinary limit/tensor comparison. It identifies the entire functorial Roos triangles, including the connecting arrows, under the canonical derived-product comparison and the cochain shift comparison of $C$. For a strict augmented tower of complexes $z_n:M\to X_n$, its canonical derived-limit augmentation $z:M\to L_R X$ satisfies $\lambda_X C(z)=z'$, where $z':CM\to L_S C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ is induced by the termwise augmented tower $C(z_n)$. These comparisons are independent of a basis and natural in maps of entire augmented towers; no exactness of countable products of sheaves and no boundedness of the complexes are assumed.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact and conservative. Use the ordinary sheaf coefficient adjunction and tensor cancellation at the unit S-module. A finite basis identifies UF with a finite power of the identity, using tensor preservation of finite coproducts and the finite biproduct comparison. Reflect finite colimits and all small limits through U to obtain exactness and continuity of F, also levelwise on towers. This handles rank zero without nonempty-index assumptions.

The exact functor localization identifies the recorded left-derived scalar extension with D(F) by uniqueness, with its counit equation. Localize the ordinary adjunction F adjoint U. The finite-power functor is self-adjoint since finite products equal finite coproducts, so its derived functor preserves products. The derived restriction functor preserves products as a right adjoint and detects isomorphisms by homology. The induced isomorphism from derived extension followed by derived restriction to the derived finite-power functor therefore shows that derived extension preserves countable products; naturality transfers this to the recorded derived tensor functor.

Use the construction of normalized total derived inverse limit and derived evaluation from the ringed strict-tower homotopy-limit proof, for independent site and coefficient universes. Its functorial injective-term K-injective resolution constructs p and delta from the actual Roos short exact sequence. The resolution unit proves the first normalization for every tower, and SES boundary naturality proves the connecting normalization for injective-term K-injective towers.

The ordinary comparison is the canonical limit projection map, invertible since F preserves limits. Localize the cochain evaluation factorization to construct the normalized evaluation isomorphism. The right-derived limit is absolute, as follows from its K-injective derivability structure and computation on K-injectives; therefore its composite with D(F) is right derived. Its universal property constructs the natural comparison with the specified unit equation. Product projections and the first normalization prove the first Roos square on injective-term K-injectives, hence everywhere by naturality and resolution.

An exact functor carries the actual SES boundary to the image SES boundary, with the standard localization and cochain shift comparisons: cancel the cone-to-third-object quasi-isomorphism, use Mathlib mappingCone.map_δ and mapHomologicalComplexIso_hom_descShortComplex, and the shift compatibility of mapDerivedCategoryFactors. This proves the assertion directly for every SES, without choosing splittings. The ordinary limit and product comparisons form an isomorphism of Roos short complexes. Hence the image of a source resolved Roos sequence is short exact even when the image tower is not K-injective.

Extend the target boundary normalization to every tower with a short exact ordinary Roos sequence by mapping to its injective-term K-injective resolution and cancelling the invertible map of derived limits. Apply it to the image resolved tower. Boundary naturality for the Roos short-complex isomorphism, the exact-functor boundary identity, and the comparison unit equation give the last Roos square on source injective-term K-injectives. Naturality then extends it to all derived towers. The middle square follows directly from product projections and additivity. No exactness of countable sheaf products is used.

These three squares form a morphism from the image source distinguished Roos triangle to the target triangle. Both product components are the same canonical comparison isomorphism. The triangulated five lemma makes the limit comparison invertible. Compose the unit normalization with an arbitrary strict augmentation; naturality of the exact-functor localization gives its required augmentation equation. Naturality of the comparison and the right-derived unit gives naturality for a map of entire augmented towers. Basis choices occur only in proving invertibility, not in defining any comparison.
